candidates.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
candidates.reason: Consistently reported as packed with no free seating by early-mid afternoon; a curated tourist food hall, not where Lisboetas eat day to day — fine as a fast, early (pre-noon) lunch stop, not the 'where people actually eat' pick this trip wants.

candidates.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
candidates.reason: Genuinely excellent per Portuguese food press, but it's the default canonical pick every guide already leads with (Pass A territory); Pass B's job is the alternative, so effort was redirected to neighborhood tascas per the traveler's explicit ask to eat where locals eat.

candidates.name: Rua Augusta Restaurant Strip
candidates.reason: Portuguese travel press repeatedly flags the Praça do Comércio / Restauradores / Figueira / Rossio / Rua Augusta cluster for above-average prices, below-average quality, and street touts handing out menus — a textbook tourist-trap signal; steer the whole cluster out of the guide.

candidates.name: Taberna Os Papagaios
candidates.reason: Portuguese press (Visão, May 2025) profiles it as part of a new wave of neighborhood tascas in Arroios (no wifi, no reservations, community-focused). Promising, but press coverage isn't a firsthand account, so it isn't independently corroborated — kept as a lead for reconcile rather than shipped.

candidates.name: A Adega do Domingos
candidates.reason: Search-preview-only lead (the native source, Lisboa Secreta, blocked on direct fetch) describing it as an unpretentious, tradition-holding tasca on Rua de Arroios near Anjos. Not independently verified — flagged as a lead only.

candidates.name: Café Santiago
candidates.reason: The benchmark francesinha and genuinely good, but queues run through lunch and dinner and it draws mostly first-timers; kept as a comparison point rather than the pick, since Bufete Fase gives a distinct version of the same dish with a neighborhood crowd and no line.

candidates.name: Porto Ribeira Waterfront Restaurants
candidates.reason: Two independent Porto-based food writers (goaskalocal.com, portoalities.com) both single out the Cais da Ribeira promenade as the city's clearest tourist-trap cluster — laminated photo menus, touts, inflated prices, thinner francesinha sauce; steer at least two streets back.

candidates.name: Casa Expresso
candidates.reason: Single local-guide source (goaskalocal.com) describing traditional dishes 'other restaurants have forgotten'; promising but only one firsthand account — kept as a lead rather than shortlisted.

candidates.name: Papagaio
candidates.reason: Same single-source lead (goaskalocal.com) — 'half-hidden, almost all-Portuguese clientele'. Not independently corroborated.

candidates.name: Quinta da Regaleira
candidates.reason: The default marquee garden and worth including, but multiple sources agree it's as crowded as Pena by mid-morning. Pass B's contribution is routing part of the Sintra day to the calmer Monserrate instead of stacking a second crowded stop — not replacing Regaleira outright; left for reconcile to weigh against Pass A's own coverage.

candidates.name: Livraria Lello
candidates.reason: Ticket price (~€15.95, redeemable against a book) only reached via search-preview, not a fetched official page (tickets.livrarialello.pt returned no readable content on fetch) — flagged for Pass A to confirm against the operator page directly rather than shipped unverified here.

candidates.name: Castelo de São Jorge
candidates.reason: 'Go at opening or after 18:00' crowd advice is widely repeated, but every source found reads as generic, near-identically-phrased listicle content rather than a distinct firsthand account — not corroborated to the bar for a shipped crowd note. Objective hours/price left to Pass A.

candidates.name: Parque da Cidade e Foz do Douro
Douro Valley Day Trip
candidates.reason: Not among the trip's stated cities (Lisbon, Porto, Sintra only); a proper Douro Valley visit needs the better part of a day plus 2+ hours' transit each way, which the itinerary as scoped doesn't budget. Flagged as a future-trip lead, not this one.

evidence.claim: Pena Palace is calmest in the first entry slots after opening; crowds build steadily through mid-morning and stay heavy into mid-afternoon (roughly 10:30-15:00) as day-trip trains, tour buses, and cruise excursions converge, then thin out again after about 16:00.

Pena Palace is calmest in the first entry slots after opening; crowds build steadily through mid-morning and stay heavy into mid-afternoon (roughly 10:30-15:00) as day-trip trains, tour buses, and cruise excursions converge, then thin out again after about 16:00.

Adult (18-64) tickets at Park and National Palace of Pena: Park-only €12; combined Park + Palace ('Essential visit') €20. Park opens 09:00-19:00 (last admission 18:00); Palace interior 09:30-18:30 (last admission ~17:30-18:00). Palace interior entry uses a timed booking slot.

Monserrate draws far fewer visitors than Pena Palace or Quinta da Regaleira — it sits off the Sintra bus-434 tourist loop, so even during peak season it's realistic to walk the palace rooms with only a handful of other visitors, versus needing to wait for a parking space at Pena.

Monserrate draws far fewer visitors than Pena Palace or Quinta da Regaleira — after a crowded morning at Regaleira, Monserrate offers a markedly slower, quieter afternoon with room to actually linger in the gardens.
Combined Park + Palace of Monserrate adult ticket (18-64): €12. Park 09:00-19:00 (last admission 18:00); Palace 09:30-18:00 (last admission 17:00-17:30).
Convent of the Capuchos adult ticket (18-64): €11. Open 09:00-17:30, last admission 17:00.

Leaving Lisbon (Rossio station) on a train before about 09:00 puts you at Sintra's main sights well ahead of the day-tripper wave; the circular tourist bus (434) gets crowded enough by mid-morning that it's worth letting one pass to get a seat rather than boarding standing-room-only.
Arriving in Sintra before 09:00 rather than 11:00 means sharing the castle/palace grounds with roughly a thousand fewer people, since summer crowds are worst from about 10:00 to 16:00.

CP's Alfa Pendular Lisbon-Porto service sells 'Promo' fares (bookable 5-60 days ahead, discounted, non-refundable) alongside refundable 'Normal' fares in 1st/2nd class; seats are assigned by carriage/number (ID required at boarding), and luggage rides with you — a small overhead rack per seat plus a shared rack near each carriage entrance, no separate baggage car.

Restaurants directly on the Cais da Ribeira promenade are consistently identified by Porto-based food writers as the city's clearest tourist-trap cluster — laminated photo menus, street touts, and inflated prices are the norm; walking two streets back (toward Clérigos, the Cathedral, or Bonfim) reaches genuinely local kitchens at lower prices.

Ribeira is 'a tourist area par excellence, so it has plenty of tourist traps' — most restaurants there are 'all icing, no cake, and expensive too'; the genuinely good venues (traditional Portuguese, seafood, fine dining) sit just off the promenade, not on it.

Bufete Fase is a small, cash-only lunch counter off the tourist path — a distinct broth-based francesinha sauce (lighter on tomato, built on a secret meat broth) served to a crowd of regulars and office workers rather than tour groups, in contrast to Café Santiago's queues down the street.

The line visible outside Pastéis de Belém is almost always the takeaway queue; walking in through the main entrance and asking staff for a table reaches a 1,000+ seat dine-in room with a wait usually under 10 minutes, even at peak times — a way to skip the queue most visitors assume is unavoidable.

Manteigaria (Chiado) and Pastéis de Belém are close enough in quality that queue length, tourist density, and travel time matter more than the taste difference; Manteigaria has no real line and sits centrally, while Belém is worth the trip mainly if already visiting the monastery.

reservations.notApplicableReason: Pass B's finds are neighborhood tascas, counter-service pastelarias, and walk-in-friendly spots (Bufete Fase, Manteigaria, the Belém dine-in room) specifically because they don't gate on reservations; no Pass B candidate rose to anchor/serious-finalist status requiring booking-window research — that belongs to Pass A's canonical picks.

transport.notApplicableReason: Both routes researched (Rossio-Sintra suburban rail, Lisbon-Porto Alfa Pendular) are high-frequency scheduled services with no single point of failure; crowd timing is worth noting but neither carries R3+ missed-connection or stranding risk in this pass.

saturation.note: ~35 native-first and English searches/fetches across Lisbon/Porto neighborhood dining, Sintra palace crowd timing, transit reality, and resident phrases. The last several rounds returned the same aggregator listicles and SEO-templated comparisons, or hit blocked sources (reddit.com, tripadvisor.com, fodors.com, lisboasecreta.co, evasoes.pt, tickets.livrarialello.pt) rather than novel firsthand leads — a clear duplicate/blocked plateau. Remaining open threads (Livraria Lello's exact ticket price, deeper corroboration on Café Santiago's queue length) are minor and non-recommendation-changing; flagged for Pass A/reconcile rather than chased further.

nativeLanguage.why: No src/data/destinations/portugal.json exists yet for this guide, so language was inferred from the destination (Portuguese) rather than read from a t0Domains list. English-only queries for Lisbon/Porto dining return the same tourist top-10 and SEO listicles every time; Portuguese-language queries (onde comer, tascas, evitar turistas, bairro Anjos/Arroios, gírias portuguesas) and Spanish-language queries for Sintra (the next-best-indexed Romance-language traveler community after Portuguese) surfaced neighborhood-specific finds and local press coverage that pure English search missed entirely.

Portuguese-language crowd/experience queries (Time Out Market, Castelo de São Jorge, Cabo da Roca, Livraria Lello)
Portuguese-language food-comparison queries (Manteigaria vs Pastéis de Belém, francesinha)

nativeLanguage.yield: Surfaced Lisbon's Arroios/Anjos neighborhood-tasca wave (Visão press coverage, a search-preview-only Lisboa Secreta lead), the Ribeira/Rua Augusta tourist-trap warning repeated across Portuguese travel press and two independent Porto food bloggers, and the Café Santiago vs Bufete Fase local/tourist split. Native-language reddit/forum threads (r/portugal, r/Lisbon) could not be fetched directly — WebFetch blocks reddit.com outright — so those stayed leads-only via search snippets rather than fetched, citable sources; several other native/local pages (lisboasecreta.co, evasoes.pt, tripadvisor.com, fodors.com) returned 403s and were marked blocked rather than promoted to citations. yt-dlp was not available in this environment, so the usual YouTube-transcript social/video aide was skipped per the tool-missing doctrine — no video/social leads were pursued this pass.
